notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Qualify the company before making assumptions about its data.
intro: A proposed sourcing workbench for Replay: organize enterprise research around operating history, relevant systems and the right business owner, then hand off a grounded discovery brief.
queueIntro: Public company context can support discovery. It does not establish ownership, licensing rights, permitted uses, data value or the absence of sensitive information.
workbenchIntro: Review fit and provenance before a seller conversation. This portfolio never exports data, assigns a valuation or authorizes licensing.
firstBody: Research an organization’s operating context, record what is known and unknown, and route legal, privacy and technical questions to their responsible reviewers.

fields.label: Operating history and company segment researched
Relevant system categories identified from a source

rules.title: Research the operating context
rules.next: Establish a company-level fit hypothesis without assuming how much usable data exists.

rules.title: Identify relevant system categories
rules.next: Use a public source or discovery question; do not request or infer private data access.

rules.title: Attach research provenance
rules.next: A company attribute needs a source and date before it supports personalization.

rules.title: Find the appropriate business owner
rules.next: Identify who can discuss the company’s operating context and route specialist questions.

rules.title: Route the issue to specialist review
rules.next: Do not treat de-identification as assumed or promise that data is safe to license. No data is collected here.

rules.title: Keep rights review explicit
rules.next: A seller must not substitute a fit score for an appropriate rights and permitted-use review.

rules.title: Preserve the existing account relationship
rules.next: Check ownership and active conversations before creating a duplicate outreach motion.

ready.title: Ready for a company-level discovery review
ready.next: The seller can ask a grounded operating-context question. Unknown rights, data value and permitted uses remain unresolved; this is not licensing approval.

experiments.name: Context-rich company sourcing
experiments.hypothesis: A grounded operating question creates more relevant discovery.
experiments.treatment: Operating history, system categories and a business question
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Owned lead handoff
experiments.hypothesis: A seller can act when fit, evidence and unresolved questions travel together.
experiments.treatment: Source-backed brief with owner and review flags
experiments.primary: Accepted qualified leads per reviewed company
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Define a qualified sourcing record
roadmap.body: Agree with AEs and SDRs on company fit, data provenance and the boundary between discovery and specialist review.

roadmap.title: Build the reliable research path
roadmap.body: Add deduplication, owned handoffs and visible pipeline failures. Keep outreach preferences and current relationships intact.
roadmap.measure: System uptime, duplicate prevention and accepted briefs

roadmap.title: Connect infrastructure to outcomes
roadmap.body: Compare sourced cohorts through held discovery and qualified opportunities, and improve tools using rep feedback.
roadmap.measure: Qualified leads, conversion and team adoption

metricsTitle: Qualified sourcing is a sequence of observable states.
metricsIntro: Synthetic operational counts keep research volume separate from accepted leads and licensing outcomes.

rows: Business context and next step confirmed
Open review flag, not an approved transaction

metricsNotes: A seller-accepted lead is not proof of data ownership, permitted use, value or a completed license.
Count unique companies and preserve the account key across enrichment and outbound systems.
Track failed or stale research jobs as operational exceptions instead of silently counting them as complete.
aiApplication: At Replay, I would coordinate public-source research around a concrete data-opportunity question, keeping unknowns explicit. A bounded review loop would route privacy, legal and technical exceptions to their owners before any proposed external action.
